name: Etoricoxib
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Etoricoxib is a selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitor. Like other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) it can reduce kidney blood flow, cause fluid retention, hypertension and hyperkalemia, and precipitate acute kidney injury. The European label needs no dose change at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 30 mL/min or above but contraindicates it below 30 mL/min. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses estimated creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min).

bands.recommendation: Usual dose by indication (30 to 120 mg once daily; see Dosing). Shortest duration at the lowest effective dose (SmPC).

CrCl ≥30: no dose adjustment (SmPC). Kidney impairment raises the risk of further decline; monitor kidney function, blood pressure and potassium, keep the patient hydrated and avoid combining with diuretics, ACE inhibitors or ARBs where possible.

hd.text: Contraindicated (CrCl <30; SmPC). Pharmacokinetics in hemodialysis were similar to healthy subjects, and hemodialysis clearance (about 50 mL/min) removes little drug, but the contraindication still applies.

pd.text: Contraindicated (CrCl <30; SmPC). Removal by peritoneal dialysis unknown. NSAIDs can also hasten loss of residual kidney function.

crrt.text: Not appropriate: contraindicated at CrCl <30 (SmPC); NSAIDs worsen acute kidney injury.

dialyzable: No: not dialyzable by hemodialysis; peritoneal dialysis removal unknown (SmPC 4.9, 5.2).
monitoring: Kidney function and potassium in patients with reduced kidney perfusion, heart failure or cirrhosis, and after starting diuretics, ACE inhibitors or ARBs. Blood pressure within 2 weeks of starting and periodically. Edema and heart failure. Liver tests if symptoms (SmPC 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Contraindicated under 16 years; adolescents 16 years and older as adults (SmPC).

renal.recommendation: Contraindicated under 16 years; adolescents 16 years and older follow adult kidney rules (contraindicated if CrCl <30).
